newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won ends edge lower on dollar/yen strength.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won ends edge lower on dollar/yen strength.

text.p: The won lost a little ground against the U.S. unit on Tuesday due to the dollar/yen strength on world markets, traders said.
The Bank of Korea was seen selling dollars in three- and six-month forward trading in the afternoon, which froze sentiment and trapped the won in a narrow range, they added.
The BOK refused to comment on talk of intervention.
The naming of a new prime minister had no impact on the market, they said.
The won closed at 864.40, against an opening high of 864.10. It touched a low of 864.80. The won closed at 863.40 on Monday.

"Most players were worried about further intervention, so they couldn't purchase dollars, but the dollar/yen was higher, so they couldn't sell. So they didn't do anything," said a foreign bank dealer.
The dollar rose to as high as 121.70 yen by midday trading.
President Kim Young-sam named Koh Kun, a former mayor of Seoul, as his new premier in Tuesday morning.
Traders said the dollar/won rate was seen moving in a similarly narrow range on Wednesday. The base mid-rate would be pegged at 864.50, against Tuesday's 863.60.
